pipeline: creative direction + implementation self-authored; cross-family (Codex) critique; repair pass driven by that critique

a11y-lint.note:
One heading-skip warning (h2->h4 in footer) surfaced on the first pass and was fixed by converting the footer group labels from

to non-heading

text — they were visual labels, not document-outline headings.

taste-lint.note: All 13 remaining findings are the warning-only Layout check `container-nesting-depth`, flagging the section > .wrap > component wrapper pattern used consistently across the page for max-width containment. This is a structural, intentional pattern (not un-authored depth) and the rubric documents the check as advisory, not a hard ceiling. Two blocking ERROR findings appeared mid-repair (`italic-display-heading`, triggered by <em> tags used for accent-color emphasis in the H1/H2) and were fixed by switching to non-semantic <span class="accent-word"> — the rubric's own prescribed cure ('carry emphasis with weight, accent color, or a drawn underline', not italics).

ds-usage-lint.note: This is a standalone marketing page with no compiled project design system (no design/ directory, no token registry) for ds-usage-lint to check usage against. Per the pipeline instructions, recorded as not applicable rather than run.

cross_family_critique.note: Codex rendered the page itself (Playwright screenshots at 1440/390/820) and read the HTML/CSS/JS before critiquing, rather than judging from source alone.

repair_pass.instruction_source: critique-codex.md verbatim — no self-directed taste changes were made outside what Codex's findings required or directly motivated

findings_addressed.finding: Final 'Start a trial' CTA pointed to '#'; every 'docs' link pointed to nonexistent '#docs'.
findings_addressed.change: Replaced the dead final CTA with a real client-side trial-request form (email input, HTML5 validation, an explicit invalid state and an explicit success state, no network call — appropriate for a page with no backend in scope). Every 'View the docs' link now points to #config-sample, a real anchor on the existing hero code panel. Footer link list was rebuilt to contain only real in-page anchors (Features, How it works, Config format, The release rule, Start a trial) instead of placeholder Docs/Changelog/Status/About/Contact/Careers links that went nowhere.

findings_addressed.finding: The large feature-card decorative visualization overlapped the 'Release trains' heading on mobile (absolutely positioned, no reserved space).
findings_addressed.change: The decorative chart (aria-hidden, non-essential) is now hidden below 860px instead of absolutely overlapping card content; it only renders at the width where the card has the extra height (min-height bump, also moved into the same 860px breakpoint) to hold it without collision.

findings_addressed.finding: Mobile menu's open state survived a resize into desktop width.
findings_addressed.change: Moved `.mobile-menu[data-open="true"] { display:flex }` inside the same max-width:860px media query as the base display:none rule, so widening the viewport always wins back to hidden regardless of stale state. Also added a matchMedia('(max-width:860px)') change listener in script.js that force-closes the menu the moment the breakpoint is crossed, as defense in depth.

findings_addressed.finding: Proof-stats + anonymous testimonial read as fabricated evidence (precise numbers with no source; unnamed persona quote presented as a customer testimonial).
findings_addressed.change: Stats band rewritten from claimed-usage numbers ('1,200+ deploys/week', '38 teams') to product-mechanism characteristics that are true by construction of the design, not asserted measurements ('Weekly / nightly' cadence, 'Zero-touch' rollback, 'In-place' adoption). The pull-quote was reframed from an anonymous customer/employee testimonial to the product's own stated release rule ('The rule Cadence enforces, not just suggests') — same layout and voice, but it no longer impersonates an unverifiable third party.

findings_addressed.finding: Desktop spacing tokens (128px section padding) used unchanged on mobile, padding the page out to 6,300+px.
findings_addressed.change: Added responsive overrides for .hero, .section, .quote, .cta-band padding-block (roughly halved below 720px, full value restored at 720px+). Measured effect: full-page height at 390px width dropped from 6,386px to 5,800px (~9% shorter) with the same content.

findings_addressed.finding: Mobile menu was a bare visibility toggle: no Escape-to-close, no outside-click-to-close, no focus return.
findings_addressed.change: script.js now closes the menu on Escape (returning focus to the toggle button), closes it on any click outside the nav/menu, and always resets aria-expanded/aria-label/icon state consistently through one setMenuOpen() function instead of duplicated toggle logic.

findings_addressed.finding: CTA-band 'pulse' graphic was literally a flat horizontal line (every point at y=60) — looked broken/abandoned next to the real pulse graphics elsewhere.
findings_addressed.change: Redrawn as three diminishing pulses that settle into a flat line — an intentional 'the beat resolves' visual, consistent with the pulse motif established in the hero and timeline instead of contradicting it.

findings_addressed.finding: Feature cards got a hover lift + shadow despite not being links or buttons — false click affordance.
findings_addressed.change: Hover effect reduced to a border-color shift only; removed translateY and the growing shadow.

findings_addressed.finding: Bento visualization SVG used preserveAspectRatio="none" inside fixed absolute bounds, distorting proportions across widths.
findings_addressed.change: Changed to preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet" so the graphic keeps its own proportions and letterboxes instead of stretching.

findings_addressed.finding: Typography is an unmodified system-sans/system-mono pairing with conventional sizing — no distinctive voice, reads like a starter template.
findings_addressed.reason: Partially addressed, not fully: added an accent-color word treatment in the H1 ('rhythm') and CTA H2 ('beat'), tying the typographic emphasis directly to the pulse/rhythm concept rather than leaving it purely conventional. Declined to go further (e.g. embedding a distinctive display typeface) because the brief requires offline file:// rendering with no CDN and no remote fonts (design-brief.json 'surface.rendering'), and embedding a full third-party font file as a base64 data URI would introduce unverified font licensing/provenance risk that generation-craft-defaults' asset-provenance discipline exists to prevent. System-font-only was a load-bearing constraint, not an oversight, so this finding is only partially resolved by design.

manual_verification: Playwright render at 390/820/1440px: no horizontal overflow at any width (scrollWidth === clientWidth).
Mobile menu opens at 390px, force-closes on programmatic resize to 1000px.

Trial form: invalid email shows an inline error and keeps focus in the field; valid email shows a success message and disables the form (no network request made, verified by design — the handler never constructs a fetch/XHR).
All in-page href="#..." anchors resolve to an existing id on the page (grep-verified: no dead fragment links remain).

blinding_check: index.html contains no comment, meta tag, class name, or copy referencing any model, vendor, tool, generator, DESIGN:OS, or AI.
